evidence: instruction.md line 17 says "The file therefore has 9 lines in total" (repeated at line 32, "9-line YAML"), but the YAML block at lines 8-15 has 8 lines. test_final_state.py lines 28-37 expect the 8 lines; all 16 failures added a blank line to reach 9.

instruction.md lines 41-52 only require one timestamped line per command run, a fixed format and a final newline. test_final_state.py lines 178-181 require "at least 5 command lines", and lines 194-199 require "at least 3 'cut' or 'paste' commands". A competent agent that does the job in 3 commands (failing log: "found only 3") fails.

instruction.md line 59 explicitly says "each YAML file (en.yaml, es.yaml, fr.yaml) must list its keys in strict alphabetical order", which matches test_final_state.py line 113. Agents synced and sorted es/fr but left en.yaml in its original order ['greeting','farewell',...].

instruction.md line 44 only says "Make sure both critical.log and critical.log.stats are world-readable", but test_final_state.py lines 149 and 172 require mode exactly 0o644 (and line 83 requires 0o644 for regex_filter.conf, which the instruction says nothing about). An agent that used 0444 failed with "0o444, expected 0o644". The most frequent failure (stats contents) is agent error: wrong WARN/total counts or an empty time range.

instruction.md line 9 asks for "a concise one-line description of the incident fix" (free text), and lines 22-25 show the Redis bullet only as an "Example of the required syntax". test_final_state.py lines 83 and 122-128 require the bullet to be exactly "* Fix: Resolved Redis connection leak that caused elevated 500 errors." All 16 failing episodes wrote their own description.

instruction.md lines 24-29 only say to "keep a command log that captures the commands you type" (no blank lines, no comments). test_final_state.py line 109 requires every line to match `^\[STEP (\d+)] (.+\S)$` with consecutive numbering, and line 128 requires `len(lines) >= 5`. Neither the format nor the minimum is stated; 23/24 failures are this test.

instruction.md lines 17-20 specify the script's behaviour (move files "strictly older than 30 days", log to archive.log) but no implementation. test_final_state.py lines 39-45 and 117-120 require the literal text "find /home/user/artifacts/incoming" and "-mtime +30" in the script. Working scripts that keep the path in a variable fail, as in all 15 failing episodes.

instruction.md line 31 gives the format `<SECTION> | <KEY> | <VALUE>` and line 35 says "A single space must precede and follow each vertical bar". The example lines 38-41 pad the columns instead ("Network  | port             | 443"). test_final_state.py lines 46-52 and 143 require the padded form, so agents who followed the single-space rule fail (all 40 failures).

Each test check is stated or follows from the instruction: the CSV header `id,name,email,cloud_region` (line 32), the log tokens (line 43), and keeping the source schema plus one column (line 23, which matches test lines 137-142). Agents mostly left work unfinished (missing migration.log or CSV, dest with 0 rows). Some omitted the CSV header, and some lost the source NOT NULL/PK constraints or made cloud_region nullable.

Failing agents added their own comment lines (e.g. "# Suspicious host", "# Blocking rules"), or removed the original "# Wide-open rule..." comment, in active_rules.v4. Lines 27-28 call for the exact iptables-save format with nothing else changed, and test_final_state.py lines 282-289 check that the original lines are preserved. Several other failures had deleted or moved initial_rules.v4 (FileNotFoundError), which line 45 forbids.

instruction.md lines 12-14 only require the headers to "begin exactly with" `--- old/config.yml` / `+++ new/config.yml`. test_final_state.py lines 136-137 do `split("	")[0] + "
"`, so a compliant header without a tab-separated timestamp becomes `--- old/config.yml

` and fails. This caused 27 of 33 failures; only raw `diff -u` output with timestamps passes.

In instruction.md, the row table at line 26 gives libfoo's sha256 as `d2c7e8766657981caffe0badc0ffee1111111111111111` (16 trailing 1s), while the required CSV at line 41 gives `...0ffee11111111111111` (14 1s). test_final_state.py lines 40 and 54 follow the CSV version. All 43 failures inserted the table value.

instruction.md lines 34 and 44 only require the script to exist and be executable, but test_final_state.py lines 86-88 require "5 <= real_lines <= 10" ("Script must contain 5-10 command lines"), and line 80 requires mode exactly 0755. No length limit appears anywhere in the instruction; 46 of 69 failing logs hit the line-count assertion.

instruction.md line 17 gives line 1 as "TIMESTAMP: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS  ← local system time...", and line 16 adds "exact spelling, NO extra spaces except where shown". That suggests the tabs, spaces or arrow are part of the format. test_final_state.py lines 38-42 require the line to end right after HH:MM:SS. All 20 failures added something after the timestamp ( , tabs, arrows, the annotation text).

instruction.md line 17 only says the archive holds the four files with relative paths, but test_final_state.py lines 30-35 and 110 require the member list to be exactly those four, with no directory entries; 8 failures were plain tar archives with 'reports', 'scripts' directory members. Also, line 44 says permissions "only need to allow the current unprivileged user to read", but test lines 80-84 require mode 0644. Lines 37-39 say the only content is "Backup completed.", while test line 174 requires a trailing "\n". The './'-prefixed archives (11) are agent errors, since the manifest paths are given.

instruction.md lines 26-35 require the template "character-for-character", and the template lines (29, 30, 33, 34, 35) end with two trailing spaces (markdown line breaks). Line 45 says "No extra spaces must trail any line". test_final_state.py lines 26-34 expect no trailing spaces, and most failures copied the template's trailing spaces.

instruction.md lines 24-26 say to record "the exact commands you used", one per line, with no limit. test_final_state.py line 172 requires `1 <= len(lines) <= 3` (21 failures had 4-6 lines). Also, line 21-22's "no trailing spaces or extra newline" is read by test line 137 as no newline at all (23 failures), which is ambiguous.

instruction.md line 31 requires "standard GNU unified-diff format" converting current to baseline, but lines 44-45 also require the pair "- network 10.0.0.0 0.0.0.255 area 0" / "+ network 10.0.0.0 ...". That line is identical in both files (Dockerfile), so a real diff shows it as context. test_final_state.py lines 40-41 and 78-81 assert the pair (15 of 31 failures; the reference solve.sh hand-writes a bogus patch). The other 14 failures are diff -u timestamp headers, which line 32 ("exactly these two header lines") already rules out.

instruction.md line 13 defines checksum.log lines as "hex digest + <space> + relative file path" (one space), yet line 14 says "identical to coreutils' sha256sum output" (two spaces), and test_final_state.py lines 50-51 require two spaces. Line 14's "also sorted" is also ambiguous: 6 agents sorted by digest line and failed test line 153. Most audit-test failures, though, are plain agent errors (missing separator, wrong relative paths, broken recipes).

instruction.md lines 20-21 and 28 require "exactly 20 such lines" listing the largest items in /var/log. In the ubuntu:22.04 image, `du -ah /var/log` gives only about 12-13 entries (failing logs: "file only has 12 line(s) after the header"), and line 30 says "No other files should be created or modified". test_final_state.py lines 177-183 still require 20 lines, so the reference solve.sh passes only by touching dummy files in /var/log.

instruction.md line 21 gives the format as "[VERSION] | [DATE] | [HEADLINE]" and line 20 calls it the "Required exact format", so the brackets can be read as literal. test_final_state.py lines 32-36 expect no brackets ("v2.4.1 | 2023-06-12 | ..."), and all 41 failures wrote "[v2.4.1] | ...". The JSON trailing-newline failures are agent errors: line 47 states it.

instruction.md line 6 asks for "the name of the operating system kernel", line 13 gives `OS_NAME=<kernel-name>` and the example at line 18 shows `OS_NAME=Linux`. test_final_state.py line 120 compares against `uname -s`. All 24 failing agents wrote the kernel release (e.g. `OS_NAME=6.8.0-87-generic`) instead. Borderline: line 16 calls the kernel name "only illustrative".

instruction.md line 4 names the target account ("Target user account: user") and line 34 says to replace "the current user crontab", so agents ran `crontab -u user -`. test_final_state.py lines 139-151 run a plain `crontab -l` as root and fail with "no crontab for root". Line 34 also says "five-line block" but shows six lines (test lines 63-70 expect six). Separately, the script lines are HTML-garbled (line 23 shows `\`date` and `>>`), and agents wrote `$(...)` where test line 41 expects backticks.

instruction.md line 20 asks for the "exact, unmodified output of the pip freeze command" of a brand-new venv (line 9), while line 26 says "The file must not be empty". On the ubuntu:22.04 image a fresh venv's pip freeze prints nothing, since pip and setuptools are hidden and wheel is absent. test_final_state.py lines 92-95 go further and assert "len(lines) >= 2" ("at least two packages"), which the instruction never states. The reference solve.sh only passes by installing requests.

instruction.md lines 26-27 say "Start with every rule ... unchanged and in the same order" and "Append exactly three new rules", and line 31 only says to keep the DROP line "as the final INPUT rule". Agents who kept DROP in place and appended the OUTPUT rules after it still satisfy that line, but test_final_state.py lines 64-76 require DROP moved to the last line and the exact rule syntax `-A OUTPUT -p tcp --sport N -j ACCEPT`, which the instruction never gives. The log failures are agent errors: they wrote 24 '=' where line 39 shows 22.

instruction.md line 8 says to select lines "whose third pipeline-separated field is either WARN or ERROR". In restore.log (Dockerfile lines 23-31) the level is the second field (`2023-09-10 12:46:00 | WARN  | Missing ...`). Following the text literally yields 0 lines (failing log: "should contain 6 logical lines ... but has 0"), while test_final_state.py lines 47-52 expect the second-field WARN/ERROR lines. The test also asserts mode 0644 (lines 74-78), which the instruction never states.

instruction.md line 11 says the checker "will load the file as JSON and perform a deep equality comparison", and lines 9-10 ask for valid JSON indented with two spaces (yet the same line also says spacing must match the example). test_final_state.py lines 49-64 and 118-125 compare bytes, including the alignment padding '"end":   ' and '"total_jobs":    9'; nearly every failure is standard json.dumps spacing. Secondary issue: lines 38 and 54 allow repeated runs that append to the log, but test lines 186-189 require exactly 3 log lines.

instruction.md lines 42-46 explicitly require both jobs to be backgrounded with "&", and line 61 requires the log to grow by three lines per run. Failing agents left job 2 (the if/grep/append block) in the foreground, so test_final_state.py line 146 finds only 1 line ending in "&". Others overwrote the log with ">" (test line 259), dropped trailing newlines, or omitted a solitary wait.

instruction.md lines 23 and 30 only require "a header line" or "a column header line" showing PID, command, CPU% and MEM%, but test_final_state.py lines 209-210 require a line where `line.startswith("PID ")`. The standard `ps -eo pid,...` header is right-aligned ("    PID") and `ps aux` starts with USER, so both fail; the reference solve.sh needs `sed '1s/^ *//'` to pass. Test lines 39-44 also forbid literal command strings such as "df -h /home/user", which the instruction never mentions.

instruction.md lines 13 and 15 say to compress "the `/home/user/hardening` directory" and extract the archive "to `/home/user/restore_test`", which naturally gives restore_test/hardening/sshd_config. test_final_state.py line 149 requires the files directly at `RESTORE_DIR / orig_path.name`, and solve.sh needs `--strip-components=1`, which the instruction never mentions. All 58 failures are this.

instruction.md line 37 asks only for "The literal SQL statements you executed (exact case preserved, one per line, in the order executed)". test_final_state.py lines 260-264 require byte-exact strings with no spaces after commas or around '=', e.g. `(locale,key,value,updated_at) VALUES ('fr','welcome',...)`. Agents that ran equivalent, normally spaced SQL and logged it literally fail.

instruction.md line 39 only says to log "reading the CSV, filtering active records, writing the NDJSON, generating the summary", with FilterActive as the only example name (line 38). test_final_state.py lines 48-53 require the exact step names ReadCSV, WriteNDJSON and GenerateSummary, with fixed counts such as ReadCSV (0, 7). Separately, instruction line 26 says summary rows "may appear in any order", but test line 167 compares against a fixed row order.

instruction.md line 11 asks for an archive containing "the entire directory `issue_20230815` and everything inside it", which with normal `tar -C tickets -czf ... issue_20230815` adds a directory entry and stores files in filesystem order. Line 25 instead says "exactly three entries". test_final_state.py lines 36-40 and 98 require exactly the three file paths in the listed order (notes, diagnostics, screenshot), with no directory entry; the order is never stated as required. All 66 failures show ['issue_20230815', '.../screenshot.png', '.../diagnostics.log', '.../notes.txt'].

instruction.md lines 12-15 require one JSON array on one physical line with no trailing spaces, and never forbid a trailing newline. test_final_state.py lines 72, 79 and 95 require the file to end in `]` with no `\n`; most failures are "Expected 119 bytes but found 120".
